chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abi Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, did not make anyone dwell in the sky except a Messenger, or an Imam, or a Vizier, or a Witness, or a Just one, or a Truthful one, or a Knower, or a Believer, or a Muslim, or a God-fearing one, or a Guarded one, or a Glorifier (male/female), or a Charitable one (male/female), or a Fasting one (male/female), or a Standing one (male/female), or a Bowing one (male/female), or a Prostrating one (male/female), or a Reciter (male/female), or a Reflecting one (male/female), or a Thinking one (male/female), or a Remembering one (male/female), or a Worshipping one (male/female), or a Humble one (male/female), or a Trusting one (male/female), or a Humble one (male/female).
ai.seo_question: Who are the inhabitants of the sky according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq elaborates on the concept of *Hujjah* (divine proof), asserting that Allah never left the earth without an Imam to guide humanity, paralleling the celestial hierarchy. This narration underscores the Shia doctrine of the necessity of the Imamate, where spiritual beings and Prophets serve as intermediaries of divine knowledge and mercy. It highlights the continuity of guidance from the heavens to the earth, ensuring that the divine message remains accessible to all generations.
